status: frozen before constructing the full feature matrices or reading cross-cluster scores
purpose: Use already-spent cluster maps to determine whether the missing one-metric Weyl Hessian is carried by scale-only total baryons, nonlinear total-baryon tidal invariants, or gas-star component overlap and orientation.

sample.target_interpretation: same-catalog conventional halo reconstruction used only as a spent inverse target, not direct truth

families.scalar_scale: metric-compatible convergence/shear triplets generated by Gaussian-smoothed total baryon convergence
families.total_tidal: scalar_scale plus total-baryon gradient magnitude, traceless Hessian, and gradient-axis tensor invariants
families.component_overlap: total_tidal plus gas-star mixing, signed component contrast, cross-gradient tensor, and difference-gradient tensor invariants

fit.coefficient_rule: one real coefficient per rotationally covariant metric-compatible feature triplet; the same coefficient acts on convergence and both shear components
fit.alpha_selection: minimum symmetric leave-one-cluster-out full-field NRMSE across the two spent clusters
fit.final_diagnostic_fit: one joint coefficient vector on both spent clusters at the selected alpha

decision_rule: If component_overlap improves symmetric cross-cluster NRMSE by at least ten percent over scalar_scale and total_tidal, require the next action to contain a component-resolved covariant source before any new observations are opened.
If total_tidal clears the same margin but component_overlap does not, require a total-baryon tidal source but not a material component label.

If no family reaches 0.5 cross-cluster NRMSE or closes 25 percent of residual power in both transfer directions, the tested local invariant library is insufficient and the next mechanism must add wider environment, dynamics, or causal state rather than another local multiplier.
No result in this spent stage validates a gravity theory or authorizes an untouched holdout.
claim_boundary: Both clusters and their comparator maps were previously opened; this is mechanism discovery only.
The compact-halo comparator is a fitted reconstruction, includes external shear, and is not direct pixel truth.
Metric-compatible feature triplets enforce one scalar lens potential at this diagnostic level but are not derived from a four-dimensional action.
Feature coefficients and ridge penalties are inverse-problem diagnostics, not proposed physical constants.
Only two clusters have complete ready comparator paths, so cross-cluster transfer is necessary but not sufficient evidence of universality.
The 700 kpc baryon context omits more distant line-of-sight and environmental structure.
